title: Android (Compatibility, Mali): native memory grows without end when 3D MSAA is on and scaling_3d_scale < 1.0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (official export templates)

### System information

Google Pixel 9 Pro XL (Tensor G4, Mali GPU), Android 17 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Compatibility renderer (OpenGL ES 3), debug export

### Issue description

On Android with the Compatibility renderer, the app's native memory grows steadily and without end (about 4.5-6.4 MB per second) when **both** of these are set:
- `Viewport.msaa_3d` is on (tested with `MSAA_2X`), and
- `Viewport.scaling_3d_scale` is below 1.0 (tested with 0.53 and 0.5).

Each setting alone is flat. Godot's own memory counters (`OS.get_static_memory_usage()`, `MEMORY_STATIC`, `RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED`) stay flat while the process native heap climbs, so the growth seems to be outside Godot's allocator: driver side, or a GL object Godot does not count (perhaps a multisample/resolve buffer re-created every frame and never freed).

Minimal project below, measured on the same phone with `adb shell dumpsys meminfo <package>`:

| MRP build | Native Heap | TOTAL PSS | Godot static / video memory (own counters) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSAA 2x, scale 0.53 | 153 MB at 10 s -> 441 MB at 55 s (~6.4 MB/s, linear) | 479 -> 765 MB | flat 33.4 MB / 45.6 MB |
| MSAA off, scale 0.53 | 62.9 MB at 10 s -> 56.6 MB at 180 s (flat) | 393 -> 379 MB | flat 34.3 MB / 45.6 MB |

In our full game (3 minutes per run, one change per run):

| MSAA 3D | 3D scale | Native memory over 3 min |
|---|---|---|
| 2x | 0.53 | grows ~4.5 MB/s, no plateau |
| off | 0.53 | flat, ~217 MB |
| 2x | 1.0 | flat, ~227 MB |
| 2x | 0.5 | grows (same slope) |

The same game build on Windows (same renderer) is flat. Workaround: turn MSAA off whenever `scaling_3d_scale < 1.0`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new 3D project with the Compatibility renderer, with one camera and a few meshes that move every frame (the MRP below).
2. At start: `get_viewport().msaa_3d = Viewport.MSAA_2X` and `get_viewport().scaling_3d_scale = 0.53`.
3. Export to Android (debug) and run it on a Mali-GPU phone.
4. Every 10 s, run `adb shell dumpsys meminfo <package>`: Native Heap and TOTAL PSS climb steadily.
5. Set `MSAA_ON = false` or `SCALE = 1.0` and repeat: memory stays flat.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The project is three small files (no assets). The defaults in `project.godot` are unchanged apart from these lines:

```ini
[application]
config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7", "GL Compatibility")
[display]
window/size/viewport_width=720
window/size/viewport_height=1280
window/stretch/mode="canvas_items"
window/stretch/aspect="expand"
window/handheld/orientation=1
[rendering]
renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"
renderer/rendering_method.mobile="gl_compatibility"
textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true
```

`main.gd`:

```gdscript
extends Node3D
## Minimal reproduction: native memory grows on Android (Compatibility / GLES3, Mali) when 3D MSAA is on and
## scaling_3d_scale is below 1.0. Flip the two switches below and re-export to compare.

## Switch 1: 3D MSAA 2x on (true, shows the leak) or off (false, flat).
const MSAA_ON: bool = true
## Switch 2: 3D render scale. 0.53 shows the leak together with MSAA_ON; 1.0 is flat.
const SCALE: float = 0.53
## Seconds between memory lines in logcat (adb logcat -s godot).
const LOG_INTERVAL: float = 10.0

var _t: float = 0.0
var _next_log: float = 0.0


func _ready() -> void:
	var vp: Viewport = get_viewport()
	vp.msaa_3d = Viewport.MSAA_2X if MSAA_ON else Viewport.MSAA_DISABLED
	vp.scaling_3d_scale = SCALE
	print("MRP msaa_on=%s scale=%s" % [MSAA_ON, SCALE])


func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	# Something must draw and change every frame.
	for child: Node in get_children():
		if child is MeshInstance3D:
			(child as MeshInstance3D).rotate_y(delta)
			(child as MeshInstance3D).rotate_x(delta * 0.5)
	_t += delta
	if _t >= _next_log:
		_next_log += LOG_INTERVAL
		print("MRP t=%d static_mb=%.1f perf_static_mb=%.1f video_mem_mb=%.1f" % [
			int(_t),
			OS.get_static_memory_usage() / 1048576.0,
			Performance.get_monitor(Performance.MEMORY_STATIC) / 1048576.0,
			Performance.get_monitor(Performance.RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED) / 1048576.0])
```
